title: How credits work
content:
## What credits are

Credits are Emergent's usage currency. Every action the platform takes on your behalf—generating code, running tests, deploying to the cloud, calling external APIs—consumes a small number of credits from your account balance. This metered approach keeps costs predictable and aligns what you pay with what you actually use.

You'll see your current balance in the top-right corner of the workspace. When credits run low, you can top up or upgrade your plan at any time.

---

## What consumes credits

Credits are deducted whenever the platform performs work:

- **Code generation**  
  Each time you send a prompt and Emergent's agents write, refactor or extend your app's code, credits are consumed. The amount scales with the scope of the change and the complexity of the files touched.

- **Testing & validation**  
  Automated tests—unit tests, integration checks, visual regression scans—all consume credits. The more comprehensive the test suite, the higher the cost per run.

- **Cloud deploys**  
  Building, bundling and pushing your app to production infrastructure (including CDN invalidation and serverless edge deployment) uses credits proportional to build time and artifact size.

- **Integrations & scheduled tasks**  
  Calling third-party APIs, scheduling cron jobs and running background workers through [Integrations & scheduled tasks](/integrations-scheduled-tasks) each deduct credits based on execution duration and frequency.

- **Database operations**  
  Heavy read/write workloads against the [MongoDB database](/database-mongodb), particularly complex aggregations or large bulk inserts, incur incremental charges.

- **LLM calls via the Universal Key**  
  If you use [the Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) to let your *app* call language models at runtime, those API calls are billed through your Emergent credit balance (not your personal OpenAI or Anthropic account).

<Info title="Maxx mode uses more credits">
When you enable **Maxx mode** (the toggle in the prompt bar), Emergent agents plan more thoroughly, explore alternative implementations and run deeper validation passes. This produces higher-quality results but consumes 2–4× the credits of a standard prompt.
</Info>

---

## Credits per prompt & setting a limit

The cost of a single prompt varies widely—from a handful of credits for a small UI tweak to hundreds for a full feature with tests and deployment. The platform shows an **estimated cost** before committing large changes, so you're never surprised.

<Tip title="Cap your spending with a per-prompt limit">
In **Settings → Billing**, you can set a **maximum credits per prompt**. If an agent's plan would exceed that ceiling, Emergent will ask you to approve the overage or break the task into smaller steps. This guardrail prevents runaway costs on complex requests.
</Tip>

If you regularly work on large, multi-file features, consider raising your limit or switching to a higher-tier plan with a more generous monthly credit allowance and lower per-credit rate.

---

## Monitoring usage

The workspace sidebar displays a real-time **credit meter** showing your current balance and this month's consumption trend. Click it to open a detailed breakdown by category (generation, testing, deploy, integrations) and see which prompts or deploys were the costliest.

You'll also receive an email alert when your balance drops below 20 % of your plan's monthly allowance, giving you time to top up before hitting zero.

<Warning title="Paused projects when balance reaches zero">
If your credit balance hits zero mid-operation, in-progress builds and deploys will pause. You can resume immediately by adding credits—no work is lost, but your app won't go live until the deploy completes.
</Warning>

---

## Topping up & rollover

- **One-time top-ups** never expire; unused credits roll over indefinitely.  
- **Monthly plan credits** roll over for up to three billing cycles, then expire.  
- You can mix plan credits and top-up credits; the platform always spends expiring credits first to maximize your value.

For high-volume teams, contact support to discuss annual prepaid bundles with volume discounts.
